questions.question: After realising the deadly effects of depleting the ozone layer, under which programme was the decision taken to ban the usage of CFC?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**United Nations Environment Programme**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The decision to ban the usage of Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) was taken under the **United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)**.
 
• UNEP is responsible for coordinating responses to environmental issues within the United Nations system.
 
• It was established in 1972 following the United Nations Conference on the Human Environment in Stockholm.
 
• The Montreal Protocol, an international treaty designed to protect the ozone layer by phasing out the production of numerous substances responsible for ozone depletion, was adopted under the auspices of UNEP.
 
• The Protocol has been successful in reducing the global production of CFCs and other ozone-depleting chemicals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Montreal Protocol** was signed on 16th September 1987 and came into effect on 1st January 1989.
 
• It is considered one of the most successful environmental agreements to date, with widespread global participation.
 
• Amendments to the Protocol have been made to include additional substances and to accelerate the phase-out schedules.
 
• The **Kigali Amendment**, adopted in 2016, aims to phase down hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), which are potent greenhouse gases.
 
• UNEP continues to play a crucial role in monitoring and supporting the implementation of the Montreal Protocol.

questions.question: On cold pressing groundnut, oils are released. This indicates the presence of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fats**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Cold pressing groundnut releases **fats**, which are a major component of oils.
 
• This process does not release significant amounts of **carbohydrates, proteins, or vitamins**, which are primarily found in other parts of the groundnut.
 
• Cold pressing is a mechanical process that extracts oil without using heat, preserving the nutritional quality of the fats.
 
• Groundnut oil is commonly used in cooking and has various health benefits due to its high content of unsaturated fats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cold pressing** is a method of oil extraction that involves crushing the seed or nut and forcing out the oil without the use of heat.
 
• This method helps in retaining the natural flavor, aroma, and nutritional value of the oil.
 
• Groundnuts, also known as peanuts, are a good source of **monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats**, which are beneficial for heart health.
 
• In addition to fats, groundnuts also contain protein, fiber, vitamins, and minerals, but these are not the primary components released during cold pressing.

questions.question: In which year was the Integrated Child Development Scheme (ICDS) launched in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1975**__

__
 
• The **Integrated Child Development Scheme (ICDS)** was launched in the year **1975**.
 
• ICDS is a government program in India that provides food, preschool education, and primary healthcare to children under 6 years of age and their mothers.
 
• The scheme aims to combat child hunger and malnutrition.
 
• ICDS services are provided through a network of Anganwadi centers established mainly in rural areas, urban slums, and tribal areas.
 
• It encompasses several components including supplementary nutrition, immunization, health check-ups, and referral services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ICDS is one of the world’s largest and most unique programs for early childhood care and development.
 
• The program is sponsored by the Indian government and is supported by state governments and UNICEF.
 
• ICDS has been instrumental in improving the health and nutritional status of children in India.
 
• The scheme also focuses on the health and education of mothers, thus promoting overall family welfare.
 
• Periodic evaluations and revisions of the scheme have been undertaken to ensure its effectiveness and relevance.

questions.question: On which date did the cantonment of Meerut break out in military mutiny during the 1857 movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10 May 1857**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The military mutiny in Meerut broke out on **Sun May 10, 1857**.
 
• This event marked the beginning of the **Indian Rebellion of 1857**, also known as the First War of Indian Independence.
 
• The mutiny started with the Indian soldiers (sepoys) of the British East India Company's army.
 
• The immediate cause was the use of new rifle cartridges rumored to be greased with cow and pig fat, offending both Hindu and Muslim religious sentiments.
 
• It quickly escalated into a widespread uprising against British rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The rebellion led to the end of the East India Company's rule in India.
 
• In 1858, the administration of India was transferred to the British Crown, beginning the British Raj period.
 
• The revolt was characterized by both violent and non-violent resistance and had a profound impact on Indian society and the subsequent independence movement.
 
• Key figures in the rebellion included leaders like Rani Lakshmibai, Nana Sahib, and Bahadur Shah II.
 
• The rebellion highlighted the widespread discontent with British policies and the desire for self-governance.

questions.question: Which word has been substituted for the words 'Unity of the Nation' in the 42ⁿd Amendment Act of the Preamble of the Constitution of India?

questions.solution:

• The term **'Unity and integrity of the nation'** was substituted for 'Unity of the Nation' in the 42nd Amendment Act of the Preamble of the Constitution of India.
 
• The 42nd Amendment Act, also known as the **Constitution (Forty-second Amendment) Act, 1976**, is one of the most comprehensive amendments made to the Indian Constitution.
 
• This amendment aimed to make significant changes to the Preamble, including adding the words 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity'.
 
• The amendment sought to emphasize the importance of national unity and integrity, reflecting the country's commitment to maintaining its territorial integrity and the unity of its people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **42nd Amendment** was enacted during the Emergency period when Indira Gandhi was the Prime Minister of India.
 
• It is sometimes referred to as a "mini-Constitution" due to the extensive changes it brought about.
 
• The amendment also aimed to reduce the power of the judiciary and enhance the authority of the Parliament.
 
• However, some of its provisions were later repealed or modified by subsequent amendments, such as the 44th Amendment Act.
 
• The Preamble reflects the aspirations and values of the Constitution, serving as a guiding principle for its interpretation and implementation.

questions.question: The Arid soils are developed in the western part of which state from the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Arid soils** are primarily found in the western part of **Rajasthan**.
 
• These soils are characterized by their sandy texture, low organic matter, and high salt content, making them less fertile.
 
• Arid soils are formed under conditions of high temperature and low rainfall, typical of desert regions.
 
• The presence of calcium carbonate and gypsum in these soils often leads to the formation of a hard pan, which can restrict root growth.
 
• They require proper management practices like irrigation and fertilization to improve their productivity for agricultural use.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajasthan** is the largest state in India by area and is known for its vast Thar Desert, where arid soils are prevalent.
 
• The climate in Rajasthan varies from arid to semi-arid, with extreme temperatures and scanty rainfall.
 
• Efforts are being made to combat desertification and improve soil fertility through various soil conservation and water management techniques.
 
• The state is also exploring alternative land use practices such as agroforestry and sustainable agriculture to make better use of arid soils.

questions.question: What is the main content of the Fourth Schedule in the Constitution of India?

options.text: Allocation of seats in the Council of States
Allocation of seats in the Lok Sabha

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Allocation of seats in the Council of States**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The main content of the **Fourth Schedule** in the Constitution of India is the **allocation of seats in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha)**.
 
• The Fourth Schedule lists the number of seats allocated to each state and union territory in the Rajya Sabha.
 
• The allocation is based on the population of each state and union territory, ensuring proportional representation.
 
• This schedule helps in maintaining a balance in the representation of various states in the Rajya Sabha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.

questions.question: Before starting a 5 day and 5 night excursion, Mr. Patel provided all his students with battery powered flash lights. He also gave them some extra batteries to use as spare. Then Mr. Patel asked them whether they know how the batteries will produce electricity and help them. What do you think the correct answer to his question is?

options.text: Electricity is produced by the chemicals stored in the battery
Electricity is produced by friction between the battery and the flash light
Electricity is saved in the battery from the factory that produces it
Battery extracts electricity from the environment and passes it to the flash light

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electricity is produced by the chemicals stored in the battery**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Electricity is produced by the **chemicals stored in the battery**.
 
• Inside a battery, a chemical reaction occurs between the electrolyte and the electrodes, generating a flow of electrons.
 
• This flow of electrons is what we refer to as electricity, and it powers the flashlight when the circuit is completed.
 
• Different types of batteries use various chemical compositions, but the fundamental principle of converting chemical energy into electrical energy remains the same.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Batteries** have been a crucial innovation in portable power, allowing for the development of various battery-powered devices.
 
• The first true battery was invented by **Alessandro Volta** in 1800, known as the Voltaic Pile.
 
• Modern batteries come in many forms, including **alkaline, lithium-ion, and nickel-cadmium**, each with unique advantages and applications.
 
• Proper disposal and recycling of batteries are important to prevent environmental harm due to the chemicals they contain.
 
• Batteries are widely used in everyday items such as **remote controls, mobile phones, laptops, and electric vehicles**.

questions.question: A village is established in a region where land meets the ocean. What is this region called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Coastal Region**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A region where land meets the ocean is called a **Coastal Region**.
 
• Coastal regions are areas that are adjacent to the sea or ocean and include a variety of geographical features such as beaches, estuaries, and cliffs.
 
• These regions are often characterized by their unique ecosystems, which include diverse flora and fauna adapted to the saline environment.
 
• Coastal regions are significant for human settlement due to their access to marine resources, trade routes, and recreational opportunities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Coastal areas can be vulnerable to natural hazards such as hurricanes, tsunamis, and rising sea levels due to climate change.
 
• Human activities like coastal development, pollution, and overfishing can impact the health of coastal ecosystems.
 
• Effective coastal management practices are essential to balance development and conservation efforts in these regions.

• The Planning Commission of India was established in 1950 to oversee the implementation and formulation of the Five-Year Plans.
 
• The First Five-Year Plan laid the foundation for the subsequent plans and set the precedent for planned economic development in India.
 
• The success of the First Five-Year Plan encouraged the government to continue with the planned approach to economic development.

questions.question: The process by which molecules from a region of higher concentration move to a region of lower concentration is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**diffusion**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Diffusion** is the process by which molecules move from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration.
 
• This process is a fundamental principle in **biology, chemistry, and physics**, playing a crucial role in various natural phenomena and industrial applications.
 
• Examples of diffusion include the **spreading of perfume in a room**, the **dispersion of pollutants in the air**, and the **exchange of gases in the lungs**.
 
• Diffusion is driven by the **kinetic energy** of the molecules, which causes them to move randomly and spread out over time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Evaporation** is the process by which water changes from a liquid to a gas or vapor.
 
• **Boiling** is the rapid vaporization of a liquid, which occurs when a liquid is heated to its boiling point.
 
• **Melting** is the process by which a solid turns into a liquid when heat is applied.
 
• All these processes are different from diffusion, which specifically involves the movement of molecules from higher to lower concentration.

questions.question: Food digested in the stomach passes through the intestines so that the blood vessels can absorb essential nutrients for the functioning and growth of the body. What is this process known as?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assimilation**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Assimilation** is the process by which digested food passes through the intestines and is absorbed by the blood vessels.
 
• This process is crucial for the distribution of essential nutrients required for the body's growth and proper functioning.
 
• Assimilation ensures that nutrients reach various cells and tissues, supporting metabolic activities and overall health.
 
• The efficiency of assimilation can be affected by factors like diet, health of the digestive system, and overall metabolic rate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The human digestive system is composed of several organs including the stomach, intestines, liver, and pancreas, all of which play a role in digestion and assimilation.
 
• Enzymes and digestive juices break down food into simpler substances that can be easily absorbed.
 
• Proper hydration and a balanced diet rich in fiber can aid in efficient assimilation.
 
• Conditions like malabsorption syndromes can impair the body's ability to absorb nutrients, leading to deficiencies and health issues.
 
• Regular check-ups and a healthy lifestyle can promote optimal digestive health and nutrient assimilation.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of formation of metamorphic rocks?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Formation of Slate**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Formation of Slate** is an example of the formation of metamorphic rocks.
 
• Metamorphic rocks are formed from pre-existing rocks (igneous, sedimentary, or other metamorphic rocks) that have been transformed by high pressure, high temperature, or both, without the rock melting.
 
• Slate is formed from shale, a type of sedimentary rock, through the process of metamorphism.
 
• During the metamorphic process, the minerals in the shale re-align and recrystallize, resulting in the dense, foliated rock known as slate.
 
• Metamorphic rocks typically exhibit characteristics such as foliation, banding, and a denser, more compact structure compared to their original form.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sandstone** and **Limestone** are examples of sedimentary rocks.
 
• **Chalk** is also a type of sedimentary rock, composed primarily of calcium carbonate formed from the skeletal remains of marine organisms.
 
• The process of metamorphism can result in the formation of a variety of metamorphic rocks, such as schist, gneiss, and marble, depending on the original rock type and the specific conditions of pressure and temperature.
 
• Metamorphic rocks can be found in regions with a history of mountain-building processes, where tectonic plates have collided and generated the necessary conditions for metamorphism.

questions.question: What was the main objection against the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Constituent Assembly?

• They are intended to guide the state in the application of laws and policies, aiming at achieving social and economic democracy.
 
• The Directive Principles are enumerated in Part IV of the Indian Constitution and include guidelines for the creation of a welfare state, aiming at reducing income inequality, ensuring fair distribution of wealth, and securing a decent standard of living for all citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Constituent Assembly** was established to draft the Constitution of India and held its first session on **9th December 1946**.
 
• The Assembly included representatives from various regions and communities of India, ensuring a comprehensive and inclusive approach to the drafting process.
 
• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, known as the principal architect of the Indian Constitution, chaired the Drafting Committee.
 
• The Directive Principles were inspired by the Irish Constitution and aim to establish a just society in India.
 
• While they are not enforceable by courts, they are considered essential for the governance of the country and aim to create a framework for a welfare state.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made to address evolving needs and circumstances, as outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The principles emphasize goals such as securing an adequate means of livelihood, equitable distribution of resources, health and education, and protection of the environment.
